# Native releases

The canonical repository is `git.parano1d.org/ignotusnemo/kairos`. GitHub `proof-native/parano1d` runs the manual Platform CI and Native Release workflows. GitLab `ignotusnemo/kairos` mirrors the same source, tag, release notes and binary files. The former GitHub `ignotusnemo/kairos` mirror is unavailable and is excluded from release checks.

## Prepare

- Maintainers merge reviewed release changes from `dev` into canonical `main`, then synchronize `main` on `proof-native` and `gitlab`. Keep `dev` synchronized with any release fixes made on `main`.
- Set the workspace version and commit `.github/release-notes/vVERSION.md`. Keep each prose paragraph and list item on one physical line.
- Use the frozen mainnet legacy metadata, v2 pack, v2 pins and two legacy retirement verification keys. Matrix-free mainnet executables embed the selected ancestry proof from `noid_node/assets/mainnet-retirement.origin` and verify it locally under those keys before accepting peers. Cold synchronization must pass through an unchanged v2.0.3 peer retaining only the legacy certificate, with DNS seeds disabled and no internet access.
- Authenticate `gh` for `proof-native/parano1d`, or supply `GH_TOKEN` with access to that repository. The local publisher checks every remote's `main` before assigning a release tag.

```sh
./scripts/publish_release.sh VERSION /path/to/history-step-pack-v1 \
  --v2-pack /path/to/frozen-v2-pack \
  --v2-pins /path/to/v2-pins.env \
  --retirement-keys /path/to/verification-keys \
  --channel stable
```

The publisher runs Platform CI for the exact source commit. After success it creates one annotated tag on all four remotes, opens a draft in `proof-native`, uploads both normalized packs and starts Native Release. Both workflows run only by manual dispatch; pushes and pull requests do not start CI.

## Build and publish

Native Release verifies the tag, source version, notes, successful Platform CI run, archive digests and complete archive contents. Each platform receives the same two packs and builds with `--pack`, `--v2-pack`, `--v2-pins`, `--retirement-keys` and `--retired-history`. The legacy archive contains pinned runtime metadata without either old matrix. Rust build validation authenticates the v2 matrices and retirement keys and checks the source schedule. The tagged source supplies the mainnet retirement proof. Every node verifies the complete proof at startup, retains it for P2P serving and applies the normal HistoryStep checks to its selected State and headers. Core and the GUI sidecar use the same matrix-free daemon.

The publisher and workflow default to retired history. Pass `--with-legacy-history` to the publisher, or set the workflow's `retired_history` input to false, when reproducing a transition release. This selects the full legacy archive and omits the retired-history Cargo feature together.

Release build scripts and their host dependencies use optimization because embedding v2 material includes a full matrix authentication pass. Each native job allows up to six hours for a cold build and retains its build log and Cargo timing reports as a separate diagnostics artifact. The Cargo cache contains downloaded sources, not compiled binaries.

Linux x86-64, Linux ARM64, Windows x86-64, macOS Apple Silicon and macOS Intel each produce a Core archive and a GUI installer. The release stays a draft until all ten deliverables succeed. Publication adds the two input packs and `SHA256SUMS`, for thirteen release assets in total.

If a build fails, inspect that job before rerunning it. A changed source commit requires a new Platform CI result. Never move an already published release tag or combine assets from different release commits.

## Synchronize delivery

Download the complete published release from `proof-native` and verify every entry in `SHA256SUMS`. Copy those exact thirteen files and the committed release notes to the canonical Forgejo release and GitLab mirror. GitLab stores the files in its generic package registry and exposes them as release asset links. No platform rebuild is needed for mirroring.

Before considering publication complete, download the assets from each destination and compare their digests with the original manifest. Check the release title, notes, channel and annotated tag on every host as well. Automatic source-code archives generated by a hosting service are separate from the thirteen release assets.
